answer: A concrete mechanism: each identity must anchor to a rotating beacon of independent random selection, so nobody can pick which peers vouch for them. Reputation and stakes are held in a public vault that is slashed when coordination is detected, making a sybil cluster's cost grow with every extra head. Each agent effectively lives on its own island: reputation does not transfer between identities, so cloning a good record is impossible. This makes buying many fake agents strictly more expensive than operating one honest one.
